seo_title: Cost of Living in Batumi 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Batumi per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: A Black Sea resort with visa-free stays of 365 days, low prices and a large Russian-speaking community of freelancers. Ideal for remote work by the sea with a mild winter.
pros: Visa-free entry for 365 days — the longest in the region
The sea and palm trees at prices below Sochi
A large Russian-speaking community of freelancers and IT workers
Low taxes for sole proprietors — 1% on turnover up to 500,000 GEL
cons: Strong seasonality — a tourist boom and traffic jams in summer
Lots of rain and overcast skies in winter; heating isn't available everywhere
High humidity from the sea — hard for asthmatics

best_places.name: Old Batumi
best_places.description: 19th-century quarters between the boulevard and Piazza square — cafés, wine bars and boutiques.

best_places.name: Batumi Boulevard
best_places.description: 8 km of seafront with palm trees, bike paths and fountains — the main spot for walks.

best_places.name: Porta Coworking
best_places.description: The leading coworking space for digital nomads: meetups, events and an open space with a sea view.

best_places.name: Botanical Garden
best_places.description: One of the largest in the world, on Green Cape — subtropics and coastal views.

visa_steps.title: Visa-free entry
visa_steps.description: Up to 365 days without a visa — all you need is a passport; the stamp is issued at the border.

visa_steps.title: Personal Number (ID)
visa_steps.description: Issued at the House of Justice — needed for renting, banking and registering as a sole proprietor.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: Bank of Georgia or TBC — both open accounts for Russians and issue cards with international payments.

visa_steps.title: Small Business sole proprietorship
visa_steps.description: 1% tax on turnover up to 500,000 GEL/year — one of the most favourable schemes in the region.

visa_steps.title: Registered rental
visa_steps.description: The lease is recorded in the registry — required for long-term residence.

faq.question: How does Batumi differ from Tbilisi?
faq.answer: The sea, a milder winter, less of an IT scene and more tourists in summer. Prices are comparable.

faq.question: What is winter like in Batumi?
faq.answer: +8–12°C, lots of rain and wind off the sea. Part of the city empties out until April.

faq.question: Can you swim in Batumi?
faq.answer: The season runs from May to October, with water up to +25°C in summer. The beach is pebbly.

faq.question: Which districts are best in Batumi?
faq.answer: Old Batumi and the Boulevard — close to the action. Khimaleuri — modern complexes, quieter and cheaper.

faq.question: How is the internet in Batumi?
faq.answer: Stable fibre at 100+ Mbps for 1,500–2,500 ₽, with 4G/5G mobile across the city.

faq.question: Is Batumi good for families with children?
faq.answer: There are private Russian-speaking schools and kindergartens; for healthcare — the private MediClub Batumi clinic.

reviews.text: I moved from Tbilisi to be by the sea — a 1% sole proprietorship, a swim in the morning and the boulevard in the evening. It's overcast in winter, but that's the only downside.
We rent an apartment in a new complex with a sea view for 70,000 ₽. Our daughter goes to an international kindergarten and my husband works from a coworking space.
